The destructor was moved inline into include/daBbl_c.h: written out of line mwcc emits the synthesized D0 ahead of the written D1, so the licensed .text is not ROM-ascending and linkcheck refuses the TU; inlining restores cartridge order (D1 0x021185c0, D0 0x021185f8) and emits no homeless D2. The header also gained the leaf fBase_c operator new, so daBbl_c_classInit is a plain `return new daBbl_c();` and the 0x31c allocation, the vptr store and both member constructions are all compiler-emitted. This TU is now daBbl_c's key-function TU, so it emits the class's own _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS plus the inherited chain's -- 11 .data symbols, all dispositioned deadstrip-data in compiler_only_output. .data is NOT licensed, deliberately: the cartridge puts g_profile_BUBBLE (0x0211bec8) between this class's _ZTI (0x0211bebc) and its vtable storage (0x0211bee4), so licensing would need two disjoint .data intervals -- the same text-only shape the already-promoted siblings ov064/daBDonketu_c and ov064/daOts_c take. The ROM RTTI name daBbl_c was kept as-is; nothing was renamed.

remaining reconstruction work, recorded rather than hidden: the five hooks at 0x02118644, 0x0211873c, 0x02118760, 0x021187d0 and 0x021187ec still carry func_ov064_<addr> linker names. Four of them are provably daBbl_c members -- the .data pointer-to-member constants at 0x0211be90/0x0211be98/0x0211bea0/0x0211bea8 take their addresses, and a pointer-to-member constant can only name a member -- but the cartridge records no English name for any of them, so coining four belongs in a rename PR. They are typed against the class here (daBbl_c * receiver, daBbl_c::State * table) so they read as the members they are, and they keep extern "C" linkage because their configured symbols are unmangled. Likewise, the two daBbl_c::State tables at 0x0211c7b8 and 0x0211c7c8 are this overlay's .bss, filled by the module's own static initializer; this TU consumes them and does not own them.
